defects: Uses `∏ᶠ` (finprod), an algebraic notion that equals a junk default of 1 whenever the multiplicative support is infinite, instead of `HasProd`/topological infinite-product convergence used in gold; since infinitely many terms 1 - X^n differ from 1, the mulSupport is infinite here, so the LHS literally reduces to the constant series 1, not the actual convergent product
Statement is specialized to R = ℤ instead of gold's generic commutative (topological) ring R; drops the `[CommRing R] [TopologicalSpace R]` generality entirely

Bug in the coefficient formula: for m = 0 the predicate `(k.natAbs > 0 ∧ pentagonal k.natAbs = m) ∨ m = 0` is trivially True for every k : ℤ (not just k = 0), so the inner ∑ᶠ ranges over all of ℤ, which is not finitely supported and hence itself collapses to the junk value 0 instead of the intended coefficient 1

As a consequence of the above two issues, the asserted equality is not merely a differently-shaped version of the pentagonal number theorem but is a different, essentially trivial/incorrect statement (LHS junk-collapses to 1 while RHS's constant term junk-collapses to 0)

No use of (or reference to) an underlying topology on the power series ring, so no genuine notion of infinite-product convergence is expressed, unlike gold's `HasProd` in the `WithPiTopology` topology
